reconcile.note: Gill treats Father and Son as joint senders of the Spirit, reading John 14 and John 15's language as one shared mission rather than rival claims.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Rudolf Bultmann read the Farewell Discourse's later chapters as displaced material relative to chapter fourteen, evidence the Paraclete sayings draw on more than one source.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Rudolf Bultmann (1941), The Gospel of John: A Commentary.

sides.snippet: the Father will send in my name
sides.verseText: But the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things, and will remind you of all that I said to you.

sides.snippet: whom I will send to you from the Father
sides.verseText: \"When the Counselor has come, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will testify about me.
